parts.note: a fell is a hill or mountain, especially in northern England
to second a motion is to back it, to support it

explanation.surface: A climber on a mountain loses the lead to the second climber on the rope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'second' looks like a noun or ordinal; it is the verb meaning to support.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner who drops from first place into the pack has retreated, which is the idiom.

clue.text: Scrape with rasp round edges of diamond

indicators.note: the rasp word goes round the other letters, so they sit inside it

parts.note: a rasp is a coarse file

indicators.note: edges means only the first and last letters of the word diamond are used

explanation.surface: Someone smooths a gem by scraping it with a rasp around the edges.
explanation.walkthrough: FILE goes round DD, the first and last letters of 'diamond'.
explanation.definitionFit: To fiddle is to play a violin, often heard as scraping the bow over the strings.

indicators.note: the officer's abbreviation is filled with the merit word, holding it inside

parts.note: Lt is the abbreviation for lieutenant, an officer
to merit something is to earn it

explanation.surface: An officer is said to have collected plenty of honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gathered' is in the sense 'I gather', meaning came to know.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather a fact is to come to know it, which is a synonym of having been taught it.

clue.text: Swell party set up on base

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word for party is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: Lib is short for the Liberal party
base means low, as in base or low motives

explanation.surface: A political party is founded on solid ground, it suggests.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns LIB into BIL, which sits 'on' (above) LOW in the down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A billow is a great wave, and a swell is the heaving of the sea in waves.

clue.text: Subtly balanced, artist's source of light

indicators.note: subtly suggests the letters of balanced are worked into a cleverer arrangement

parts.note: RA stands for Royal Academician, a recognised artist

explanation.surface: A painter's lighting, carefully balanced, illuminates the canvas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Subtly' rearranges BALANCED into CANDELAB, then RA follows.
explanation.definitionFit: A branched holder for several candles is a lamp-like fitting that lights a room.

clue.text: Is Henry absorbed by dance piece?

indicators.note: the first letters are taken into the dance word, ending up inside it

parts.note: to bop is to dance
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: A question about whether a man named Henry is swept up in a piece of dance music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'piece' is a chessman, not part of the dance: a bishop moves diagonally.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess every figure on the board is called a piece, and the mitred one moving diagonally is one.

clue.text: Busybody in time gets more insolent

parts.note: ruder means more impertinent or insolent

explanation.surface: A meddler, given time, becomes ever more cheeky.
explanation.definitionFit: A busybody pushes into other people's affairs uninvited, like a meddler barging in.

clue.text: Dance involving sailors with very good energy

definitions.text: Dance involving sailors with very good energy

indicators.note: the dance word wraps around the sailors, so they sit inside it

parts.note: to hop is to dance in a lively way
RN is the Royal Navy, hence sailors
pi, short for pious, means very good or sanctimonious
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Sailors performing a lively dance with great vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a lively sailors' dance and also builds it: HO(RN)P, then PI and E.
explanation.definitionFit: The traditional solo jig associated with seamen on board ship is danced energetically.

clue.text: Garden space for allotment was inaccurate, mostly

parts.note: a part is a share or allotment

indicators.note: mostly means the last letter of the word for was inaccurate is dropped

parts.note: to err is to be wrong, so erred means was inaccurate

explanation.surface: Someone describes a garden plot on an allotment but gets most of it wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allotment' looks like the gardening plot, but it is a share. 'mostly' trims ERRED to ERRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal, level garden area with ornamental flower beds laid out in patterns is this.

clue.text: Cowboy feature picture about origin of Laramie

indicators.note: the picture word goes about the other letter, enclosing it

parts.note: a drawing is a picture

indicators.note: origin means just the first letter of the word Laramie

explanation.surface: A western film's poster depicts the town of Laramie, Wyoming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'feature' suggests a feature film; it is a characteristic. Laramie is a Wyoming town familiar from westerns.
explanation.definitionFit: A slow, lengthened speech manner is a stereotypical trait of the American cowhand.

indicators.note: losing tells us the time letter is taken out of the beginner word

parts.note: a starter is someone who begins

explanation.surface: A novice stands open-mouthed, wasting precious minutes.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone gawping looks fixedly and openly, which is what one who gazes does.

parts.note: reads as an upper-case letter, but means a person from a capital city

explanation.definitionFit: A native of England's chief city is a person of a capital, someone from the metropolis.

indicators.note: the representative is bound by, held within, the policy word

parts.note: a rule is a principle or policy
an MP, a Member of Parliament, is an elected representative

explanation.surface: An elected member is constrained by party policy and feels ruffled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bound by' reads naturally as a politician bound by policy, and it is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruffle hair or cloth is to crease and tousle it, a synonym.

clue.text: You'll need energy, it's said, moving miller's grinder

annotationWithheld.clue: You'll need energy, it's said, moving miller's grinder

clue.text: The type to harbour many a grouse?

definitions.text: The type to harbour many a grouse?

parts.words: The type to harbour many a grouse?
parts.note: reads as someone full of complaints, but means a man who protects game birds on an estate

explanation.definitionFit: On a shooting estate, the person employed to rear and protect birds for sport looks after many red grouse.

clue.text: One running off after second athlete

indicators.note: after places the running-off word behind the second letter

parts.note: a printer runs off copies

explanation.surface: Someone sprints off after the second competitor in a race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'running off' suggests fleeing; a printer runs off copies.
explanation.definitionFit: A sprinter is a track athlete who races over short distances.

parts.note: for can mean regarding or concerning, as in 'so much for that'
a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: A lock on the door is considered a form of protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lock' suggests a door lock; it is a lock of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A fortified stronghold is a defensive structure.

clue.text: Light appearance of some iron, well-wrought

indicators.note: wrought means worked or shaped, so the letters are reworked into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Something shiny appears in a piece of finely crafted iron.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-wrought' rearranges SOME IRON.
explanation.definitionFit: The rising of the moon is the appearance in the sky of its light.

parts.note: reads as a cry when landing a blow, but means an instruction to capture an image with a camera

explanation.definitionFit: Snapping a picture with a camera is 'taking' it, so the instruction asks for a snap.

definitions.meaning: a diacritical sign over a letter, such as an acute
the emphasis laid on a syllable when speaking

explanation.surface: A sign showing that a person is under strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Both a written diacritic over a vowel and the emphasis on a spoken syllable go by this name.

parts.note: Reg is a typical man's name, standing for any chap
ale is a drink

explanation.surface: A friendly fellow is bought a beer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treat' looks like a noun; it is the verb, to entertain lavishly.
explanation.definitionFit: To regale guests is to entertain them lavishly, to treat them.

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
pens are female swans

explanation.surface: Something resembles the birds perched in the trees.
explanation.walkthrough: A pen is a female swan; the male is a cob.
explanation.definitionFit: These are a kind of poplar tree with trembling leaves, so they are trees.

definitions.meaning: serious or earnest, as an earnest look
the purpose or aim one has in mind

explanation.surface: Death is final, someone gloomily remarks.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means earnestly focused as an adjective and purpose or aim as a noun.

parts.note: rackets are bats used in tennis or squash

explanation.surface: A naturalist sorts the native species of flying mammals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bats' suggests the animals; they are rackets.
explanation.definitionFit: To put things into groups or categories is to group, or classify, them.

indicators.note: we hear means a word is given by how it sounds when spoken

parts.note: a Thai person is from Thailand, in the Orient
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
in means fashionable or trendy

explanation.surface: A fashionable piece of Eastern jewellery is described softly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' makes THAI give TIE, then P and IN follow.
explanation.definitionFit: A decorative pin worn to hold a necktie in place is a piece of jewellery, an ornament.

indicators.note: the house word goes around the East letter, enclosing it

parts.note: in astrology Libra is one of the twelve houses or signs
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A free house, a pub not tied to a brewery, stands to the east of a musical note.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free house' reads as a pub not tied to a brewery; 'Free' is the definition, 'house' an astrological sign.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate someone is to set them free, a synonym.

clue.text: Took off after game, got moving

indicators.note: after puts the took-off word behind the game letters

parts.note: RU is rugby union, a game
to shed clothes is to take them off

explanation.surface: A player departed after the match, hurrying away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Took off' looks like a synonym for departing; it means removed, as clothes are shed.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who hurried got going quickly, which is to have moved in haste.

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside: the partnership letters sit outside

parts.note: G and S are Gilbert and Sullivan, the operetta partnership
litters are the broods of young that cats bear

explanation.surface: A songwriting duo, minus their famous feline musical, still shines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking', and 'Cats' like the musical; GS is Gilbert and Sullivan, wrapped around LITTERS.
explanation.definitionFit: To glitter is to shine with bright flashes of light, to sparkle.
